item.title: How Much Torah Must a Father Teach?
item.description:
What is the five-fold naming of Shavuot, and how much Torah must a father teach his child? The names, from the Torah and the Sages, lead to the father's duty from the Torah to teach his child the entire Tanakh, with Mishnah and Gemara if he has the time or means.

item.title: Talmud Torah: Grandparents, Teachers, Self Study & Women
item.description:
Who is obligated to teach Torah? Not only a father to his son: a grandfather too, and in truth every Jew with knowledge and time. One who has no teacher must teach himself. The obligation covers sons, not daughters, with women's learning left for the next day.

item.title: Can Women Learn and be Taught Torah?
item.description:
May a woman learn Torah? The source is the Mishnah in Sotah, where Ben Azai recommends teaching a daughter, while Rabbi Eliezer calls it tiflut. Rashi and the Rambam read that word differently, and the Prisha says a woman who chooses to study alone has shown she is not like the majority.

item.title: Women & Torah Learning: Why Our Approach is Different Today
item.description:
Should women learn Torah? The Rambam and Shulhan Arukh say not to teach one's daughter oral Torah, and preferably not the written either. Four caveats follow, including a woman who wants to learn herself and the Hafez Hayim's view that today women should learn Torah Shebikhtav, which some extend to Mishnah and Talmud.

item.title: Two Approaches to Torah Study: Sepharadim vs Ashkenazim - Part 2
item.description:
Should Torah study be divided into three parts? The Rambam and Shulhan Arukh divide the day among Mikra, Mishnah (final halakhah) and analysis, while Rabbenu Tam, followed by the Rama, treats Talmud Bavli as containing all three. Sephardim traditionally studied in order, beginning with Tanakh.

item.title: The Two Obligations Regarding Torah
item.description:
What exactly does the Torah require regarding Torah study? There are two separate misvot, to study Torah and to teach it. Introducing the halakhot of Talmud Torah ahead of Shavuot, the Rabbi opens with the Rambam's statement in the Shulhan Arukh that every Jewish male is obligated, however busy or poor, and that the main time for study is at night.

item.title: Taking Payment for Teaching Torah
item.description:
May a teacher take payment for teaching Torah? The Gemara, Rambam and Shulhan Arukh rule one may not charge for the teaching itself, but may be paid for the time and work forgone, which is the common practice, with payment for holding a Torah position still to be discussed.

item.title: Rabbinic and Kollel Stipends in Halacha
item.description:
May rabbis, teachers and dayanim receive a salary for Torah positions? The Rambam is strongly against taking support for Torah, calling it desecration of HaShem, while the Bet Yosef and others disagreed. The class explains the positions on stipends, including long-term kollel study, and how modern professional standards differ.

item.description:

item.title: Making Kiddush Early on Shavuot Night
item.description:
May one pray Arvit and make Kiddush early on Shavuot night, as we do on summer Fridays? Ashkenazim wait for nightfall, a view developed in the 16th and 17th centuries. Sephardim always made Kiddush after shekiah without waiting, so in London one may pray Minhah early and make Kiddush around 8:45.

item.title: Preparing for Second Day Hag on First Day
item.description:
May you prepare on the first day of Shavuot for the second night? Preparing from one holy day to the next is forbidden, so the advice is to begin the second-night meal before sunset, which allows setting the table and heating food on the afternoon beforehand.

item.title: A Brief Idea for Shavuot
item.description:
Was the Torah forced on Israel, or protected by the mountain? The Gemara says God held the mountain over them like a barrel; the Mekhilta says it shielded them from the thunder. The shiur joins the two: the coercion was an act of love, and the misvot can feel like a threat or a protection.

item.title: Dairy On Shavuot
item.description:
Where does the custom of eating dairy on Shavuot come from? Not the Torah or Talmud, but first recorded around the 14th century. One reason, the Rema's, is the two loaves, and that this does not replace eating meat on Yom Tov. The Spanish and Portuguese community never accepted it.

item.title: Earliest Time for Arbit & Kiddush on Shavuot
item.description:
What is the earliest time for Arvit and Kiddush on Shavuot, when it falls on Mosei Shabbat? In London sunset is 9:15 and nightfall about 10:15. The first of three questions is a regular year, where many Sephardim pray Arvit and say Kiddush after sunset rather than waiting for nightfall; the Mosei Shabbat complications follow next.

item.description:

item.description:

item.title: Controversy Around Trees on Shavuot
item.description:
Where does the custom of flowers and greenery on Shavuot come from? The Maharil mentions greenery in the synagogue, and the Rama links it to Sinai's grass. Some objected to trees because of their resemblance to non-Jewish practice, but flowers and trees are accepted by Sephardim and many Ashkenazim.

item.title: Shortcuts in Life
item.description:

item.title: Were We Forced to Accept Torah
item.description:
Can a heavenly voice decide the halachah? The excommunication of Rabbi Eliezer ben Hurkenos, whose proofs from a carob tree, a stream and the walls all failed, and the answer that the Torah is not in heaven. A Shavuot thought: each generation's Hakhamim interpret the Torah, and HaShem is proud when his children do so.

item.title: Women Learning Torah, Part 1
item.description:
May a woman study Torah, and what is the source for holding back? The Mishnah in Sotah has Ben Azai against Rabbi Eliezer, who calls it tiflut, which Rashi and the Rambam explain differently. The Shulhan Arukh follows Rabbi Eliezer for oral Torah, but the Maharil and the Perishah allow a woman who chooses to learn.

item.description:

The Rambam reads the second third as the whole Oral Torah, from the Mishnah to the end of the Gemara, and the last third as understanding the principles behind the halakhot.

item.title: A Thought for Shavuot: Shortcuts in Life
item.description:
Why do some stand for the Ten Commandments and others not? The Rambam says the Rabbis stopped reciting them daily so that nobody would think they replace the Torah, while others stand because they summarise it. The thought for Shavuot is that there are no shortcuts, as Hillel teaches: the rest is commentary, go and learn it.

item.title: A Thought for Shavuot: Forcing Us to Accept Torah
item.description:
Was the Torah forced on us, or were we protected? The Gemara says God held the mountain over Israel and told them to accept the Torah or be buried there, while the Mechilta says He covered them in protection from the thunder. A thought for Shavuot: both are true, since coercion was an act of love, like a parent.
